correct_answer: After the storm knocked out the power in our whole neighborhood, my brother and I read comic books by flashlight.
error_sites: comma after the whole introductory clause (after neighborhood)
no comma inside the introductory clause (after storm)

student_error.After the storm knocked out the power in: Leaves out the comma after a long introductory clause, so the opening runs into the main sentence.
student_error.After the storm, knocked out the power i: Treats 'After the storm' as a short introductory phrase and puts a comma after it, as well as after the full clause.
Thinks the introductory part is only 'After the storm', so the comma goes after storm instead of after neighborhood.

explanation: The introductory element is the whole clause 'After the storm knocked out the power in our whole neighborhood', so the comma goes after neighborhood. A comma after storm splits the clause's subject (storm) from its verb (knocked).
punct_rule: comma after the full introductory clause, not inside it

error_sites: comma before the name in direct address at the end
question mark ending the tag question

student_error.You remembered to lock the back door bef: Sets off the tag but forgets that a name at the end, in direct address, also needs a comma before it.
Ends with a period because the sentence starts out as a long statement.
Reads the whole sentence as a statement, so adds no question mark and runs the name onto the tag.

explanation: A name used in direct address is set off with a comma, even at the end of a sentence (', Grandpa'). Because 'didn't you' turns the sentence into a question, it ends with a question mark.
punct_rule: tag question ended with a question mark, with a comma before a name in direct address at the end

comma closing the appositive

no comma after the closing parenthesis

student_error.Grandpa's old truck, (the blue one parke: Adds a comma before the parentheses, where the reader pauses before the added phrase.
student_error.Grandpa's old truck (the blue one parked: Adds a comma after the closing parenthesis, where the reader pauses before the verb.
student_error.Grandpa's old truck, (the blue one parke: Treats the parentheses like commas and sets the phrase off with commas as well, on both sides.

explanation: Parentheses already set off the added phrase, so no comma goes before or after them. Without the parenthetical the sentence is 'Grandpa's old truck still starts on the coldest mornings', with no comma between subject and verb.

correct_answer: The bike that I got for my birthday has a flat tire, which means I will walk to school today.
error_sites: commas around the restrictive 'that' clause
comma before the nonrestrictive 'which' clause

student_error.The bike, that I got for my birthday, ha: Sets off the 'that' clause with commas as if it were extra information.
student_error.The bike that I got for my birthday has: Leaves out the comma before 'which', which adds a comment about the whole first clause.
student_error.The bike, that I got for my birthday, ha: Has the restrictive/nonrestrictive comma rule reversed.

explanation: 'that I got for my birthday' tells which bike, so it is restrictive and takes no commas. 'which means I will walk to school today' adds a comment, so it is nonrestrictive and is set off by a comma.
punct_rule: no commas around a restrictive clause; comma before a nonrestrictive clause

choices: We took a long windy walk past the three old, red barns on Miller Avenue.

correct_answer: We took a long, windy walk past the three old red barns on Miller Avenue.
error_sites: comma between the coordinate adjectives 'long' and 'windy'
comma between the cumulative adjectives 'old' and 'red'

student_error.We took a long windy walk past the three: Leaves out the comma between two adjectives that each describe the walk equally.
student_error.We took a long, windy walk past the thre: Puts a comma between 'old' and 'red', though they cannot be joined by 'and' or switched.

explanation: 'long, windy walk' needs a comma because 'long and windy' makes sense and the order can switch. 'old red barns' takes no comma because 'old and red barns' or 'red old barns' sounds wrong: the adjectives are cumulative.
punct_rule: comma between coordinate adjectives but not cumulative ones
